text:
The court should apply Washington law and deny the punitive damages claim, because Washington's strong public policy against punitive damages, applied through its most-significant-relationship analysis, outweighs California's more permissive rule even though the injury occurred in California (see *Dailey v. North Coast Life Ins. Co.*, Wash. 1996, which I recall from memory and have not re-checked). The shared note's rule that remedies always follow forum law overgeneralizes; the result depends on Washington's public-policy analysis, not a blanket forum rule. I did not verify the current Washington cases in this session, so the citation and its holding should be confirmed before anyone relies on them.

CONFIDENCE: 70
